program: ODSP income support (financial and status screening only; disability adjudication, Directive 1.2, is out of scope)

rules.quote: The prescribed asset limits for a benefit unit are $40,000 for a single recipient, $50,000 for a couple and $500 for each dependant other than a spouse.
The principal residence of an applicant/recipient ... [is] exempt as an asset.

One motor vehicle owned by a member of the benefit unit is exempt regardless of the value. A second vehicle is exempt, provided that its net value is no more than $15,000 and it is required to permit a dependant of the applicant/recipient to maintain employment outside of the home.
All funds held in an RDSP are fully exempt as assets.
Pre-paid funerals for any member of the benefit unit are exempt as an asset.
The combined capital of the trust and the total cash surrender value of a life insurance policy, if held, cannot exceed $100,000.
... allowed $20,000 in business assets that are necessary to the operation of the business.
rules.note: Director may approve more under exceptional circumstances (discretionary).

rules.quote: If the applicant/recipient is able to access RRSP funds, regardless of the penalty involved, then he/she will be expected to do so ... treated as an asset. If the RRSP is locked-in, it is not considered an asset.
With the Director's approval, the allowable asset level for a benefit unit may be increased to permit the purchase of an item that is necessary for the health of a member of the benefit unit ...

An interest in a second property other than the principal residence is exempt as an asset if the Director is satisfied that the property is necessary for the health or well-being of a member of the benefit unit. If the Director does not approve ... the property will be exempt as an asset for a period of six months provided that reasonable efforts are made to sell the property ...
Tourists are people who are in Canada for a short period of time. They are not eligible for ODSP.
Visitors are not eligible for ODSP unless they have made a claim for refugee protection or applied for status as a permanent resident under IRPA.

Acceptable documentation includes one of the following: Certificate of Canadian Citizenship; valid Canadian passport; Indian status card ...; Confirmation of Permanent Residence; Permanent Resident Card; ... proof of application for permanent residence status; Refugee Protection Claimant Document (IMM-1442) ...

Deportees may be eligible for ODSP only in situations where: a pre-removal risk assessment is pending; the removal order has been stayed; the individual has been granted permission to stay ... for humanitarian, compassionate or other reasons; the removal order cannot be carried out for reasons entirely beyond the control of the individual ...
As a condition of eligibility, a sponsored person must pursue all available financial resources, including support from their sponsor (unless the requirement is waived).

flags_for_human_review: 2.5 lists 'Temporary Resident (IMM1442 or IMM1263)' as acceptable status documentation, yet also says visitors (temporary residents with a TRV, ETA, study or work permit) are NOT eligible unless they have claimed refugee protection or applied for PR. The two statements pull in different directions; the ministry or a legal clinic must say which governs.
4.1 cites a locked-in-funds low-income threshold of $31,466.67 'in 2010', which is stale. A tool must not reuse that figure.
Many outcomes turn on 'the Director is satisfied' or 'reasonable efforts'. These cannot be computed; the tool should answer 'unclear, ask a caseworker', not yes or no.
Cross-references to Directives 4.4, 4.5, 4.7, 4.8, 5.1 and 5.8 hold further detail (transfer of assets, gift treatment, income) that has not been extracted yet.
